name: Gulf Oil Lubric.
why: Record quarterly sales, annual sales, annual profit
Working capital healthy - debtor days 48 to 47, inventory days 95 to 98 (not rising)
Management outlook: So, the 16% growth in a quarter in which we expected the monsoon , being a low seasonal quarter would play its role.
Credit rating AAA/Stable (ICRA) - strong balance sheet
Latest quarter Sep 2026: Good (sales +44% YoY, profit +34% YoY)
Profits backed by cash: operating cash flow is 111% of 3-year profit
Sector cycle: Earnings improving but price not confirming
risks: Margins shrinking (12% to 12%) - record profit may be near peak

guidance: So, the 16% growth in a quarter in which we expected the monsoon , being a low seasonal quarter would play its role.
So, are we expecting that to increase to, say, 100 -odd days level?
capex: So, I think for us, Tirex, as we also announced, we're going to take the capacity up to 3,000 chargers, and that will happen sometime end of this year.

Silvassa capacity expansion is progressing well, but we see that there can be some 1, 2 months of delay and the spillover may happen to Q1 of next year in terms of readiness as against our earlier target of March '27.
risks: Despite a tough situation internally in terms of cost challenges and also West Asia crisis, we have seen obviously the costs remaining what they were.
We've been able to really show the agility continued in a challenging environment.
focus: We continue our focus to also look at new customers.
And I think some of the B2B industrial customers that came in, nearly 1/3 of the i ncremental growth is from new customers.
And we also continue to focus on premiumization as part of our strategy and continue to gain momentum in these.
